name: Armoured Corps
role: Forms the backbone of the Army's mechanised strike capability with high mobility, heavy armour and overwhelming firepower.
history: The Armoured Corps is one of the premier combat arms of the Indian Army, tracing its origins to the first cavalry regiment raised in 1776.
The modern Armoured Corps was established in 1947 following India's independence, inheriting two-thirds of the personnel and assets of the British Indian Army's Indian Armoured Corps.
Popularly known as the Tank Regiment of the Indian Army, it forms the backbone of the Army's mechanised strike capability with high mobility, heavy armour and overwhelming firepower.

The Armoured Corps Centre and School is located at Ahmednagar, Maharashtra, while the President's Bodyguard serves as its senior-most regiment. The Corps currently comprises 67 armoured regiments, of which 21 have been awarded the President's Colours.

The Armoured Corps celebrates Armour Day every year on 1 May, commemorating the mechanisation of the Scinde Horse in 1938. From the Centurion and Vijayanta tanks during the 1965 and 1971 Indo-Pak Wars to today's T-72 Ajeya, T-90 Bhishma and indigenous Arjun Main Battle Tanks, the Corps continues to spearhead India's armoured warfare capabilities.
